# @zakkster/lite-aabb

> Zero-GC 2D axis-aligned bounding-box primitives. Twelve operations on a flat `Float32Array(4)` `[minX, minY, maxX, maxY]`. Every op that returns a box writes into a caller-provided `out` buffer. ~120 lines, zero deps, ESM only.

## Format

An AABB is a `Float32Array` of length 4. Indices: `0=minX`, `1=minY`, `2=maxX`, `3=maxY`. No class wrapper; module-level functions only.

## API

Single named export: `aabb2`.

```ts
aabb2.create(minX?, minY?, maxX?, maxY?): Float32Array  // ALLOCATES — setup only
aabb2.clone(a): Float32Array                            // ALLOCATES — setup only
aabb2.copy(out, a): out                                 // out ← a
aabb2.set(out, minX, minY, maxX, maxY): out             // write explicit bounds
aabb2.merge(out, a, b): out                             // out ← bbox enclosing a∪b
aabb2.extend(out, b): out                               // out grows in place to include b
aabb2.fatten(out, a, margin): out                       // expand by margin on all sides
aabb2.perimeter(a): number                              // 2 * (w + h)
aabb2.area(a): number                                   // w * h
aabb2.overlapArea(a, b): number                         // intersection area, 0 if disjoint
aabb2.intersects(a, b): boolean                         // overlap test (touching counts)
aabb2.contains(a, b): boolean                           // a fully contains b (touching counts)
```

## Rules

- `create` and `clone` allocate — call only at initialization.
- Every other function takes an `out` parameter and writes into it. None allocate.
- `out` may alias any input under any view relationship — identical view, a shifted/overlapping `subarray` of one buffer, or a distinct buffer. The writers snapshot inputs before writing (v1.0.2+; ≤1.0.1 corrupted shifted views — finding A-07).
- The `aabb2` namespace is frozen (`Object.isFrozen(aabb2) === true`); its ops are a contract, not a mutable bag.
- All predicate boundaries are inclusive (touching counts as overlap / contained), EXCEPT `overlapArea`, which returns `0` for a touching (zero-width) intersection — a touching pair shares zero area. This three-way split is deliberate.
- Use `Float32Array`, not `Array` or `number[]` — typed-array indexed reads are ~3× faster.

## When to use

- Per-frame collision broadphase in canvas / WebGL / WebGPU games.
- Bounds-tracking for sprite batchers, scroll viewports, hit-testing.
- Twitch Extension overlays where any per-frame allocation breaks the 60fps budget.
- Compatible leaf-AABB format for `@zakkster/lite-bvh` (insert / update / query).

## When not to use

- 3D bounding boxes — this is `(minX, minY, maxX, maxY)` only.
- Sub-pixel-stable simulations spanning millions of world units — `Float32` precision (~7 decimal digits) becomes limiting; swap to `Float64Array` and pay the doubled memory.
- Swept-AABB / TOI computation — use a CCD library; this package is for static bounds at a single time step.

## Install

```bash
npm i @zakkster/lite-aabb
```

```js
import { aabb2 } from '@zakkster/lite-aabb';
```
